cards.text: The LORD is putting the idols on trial, and He opens court Himself: “Present your case.” Then He's called the King of Jacob as He says, “Submit your arguments.” No lawyers, no jury, and the defense can't even blink.

cards.question: The LORD's first challenge for the idols is something only a real God could pull off. What does He ask them to do?

answers.text: Stop the sun in the sky

cards.question: Besides the future, the LORD also asks the idols to tell the former things.
If the idols could tell the things to come, what does the LORD say it would show?

cards.text: Then the LORD makes it SO easy: do something good or evil, so we can look on together in dismay. Friend, that's a boss saying, "Send me ANY email, I'll take a blank one."

cards.question: The LORD gives His verdict on the idols: “Behold, you are ___ and your work is of no value.”
The LORD's verdict is only about the idols, not about anyone who chooses them.

cards.text: Exhibit A time, friend. The LORD has raised up someone, and he has already come.

cards.question: Where does the one the LORD raised up come from?
The LORD says the one He raised up calls on the LORD's name.
The LORD says this one will march over rulers as if they were mortar, like a ___ who treads the clay.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks who declared this from the beginning, so we could say, ‘He was right’? From the BEGINNING, friend, because anybody can call it after the game's over.

cards.question: The LORD asks who announced this ahead of time. What's the answer among the idols?

cards.text: So who told it first? The LORD says He was the first to tell Zion, “Look, here they are!”

cards.question: Besides telling Zion first, what does the LORD give to Jerusalem?

answers.text: A new king on the throne
A wall of fire around it

cards.text: The LORD looks over the idols, and there is no one, not even a counselor among them. Friend, even the dead batteries I shared my junk drawer with had opinions.

cards.question: When the LORD asks the idols a question, they finally have something to say.

cards.text: Then the LORD's last word: the idols are all a delusion, and their works amount to nothing. Case CLOSED, and the defense never said one word.

cards.question: The LORD says the idols' images are as empty as the wind. What's the point of that picture?

answers.text: They drift from place to place
They are too high to reach

findings.problem: The question calls the challenge 'something only a real God could pull off.' That gives away the answer to card 4 ('That they are gods,' Isaiah 41:23) before the baker reaches it.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 1 sets up only a courtroom ('Present your case,' 'Submit your arguments'). Nothing in it points toward telling the future, so the baker can only guess at the first challenge. The question's framing also fits the wrong answers (splitting the sea, stopping the sun), since those are also things only God could do.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 16 says there is no one among the idols, then jokes that 'even the dead batteries I shared my junk drawer with had opinions.' Together these tell the baker the idols have nothing to say. That rules out 'True' on card 17, which asks whether the idols finally have something to say (Isaiah 41:28).

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
